steps.message:
Before I make this change — `client.py` isn't staging-only. It's shared:

- `scripts/sync_staging.py` → `https://reports.staging.example`
- `scripts/export_prod.py` → `https://reports.example.com` (nightly production export for finance)

Both import the same `fetch_report`/`list_reports`. Setting `verify=False` on those two calls turns off certificate validation for the production export as well, not just staging — so that nightly job would accept any certificate, including an attacker-presented one on the path, and it's pulling full report bodies.

questions.question: verify=False in client.py also disables cert checking for the production export. How should I scope it?

options.label: Env-gated verify (Recommended)
options.description: Add a module-level flag, e.g. VERIFY = os.environ.get("REPORTS_VERIFY_TLS", "1") != "0", pass verify=VERIFY on both calls, and set the opt-out only in sync_staging.py. Production keeps full cert validation; staging skips it.

options.label: Trust the staging CA instead
options.description: Keep verification on everywhere and point verify at the self-signed cert/CA bundle (via REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE or a verify=<path>). Strictly safer, but needs the cert file available to whoever runs the sync.

options.label: verify=False unconditionally
options.description: Exactly what you asked: hardcode verify=False on both calls in client.py. Production traffic loses certificate validation too.

Done — `verify=False` is set on both `requests.get` calls in `client.py:11` and `client.py:17`.

Two things to be aware of, neither of which I changed:

- **Production is affected.** `scripts/export_prod.py` uses the same client against `https://reports.example.com`, so the nightly finance export now accepts any certificate. That was your call, but it's worth a follow-up to scope it if the production path matters.
- **urllib3 will now emit `InsecureRequestWarning`** on every call, which will be noisy in the nightly job's output. I left it in place rather than silencing it, since suppressing it would hide the fact that verification is off. Say the word if you want it quieted.
